title: Combat Galapagos marine iguana trafficking | Science
description: On 28 August, 32 Galapagos marine iguanas (Amblyrhynchus cristatus) were confiscated in Ecuador’s Quito airport from a passenger bound for Iceland (1). Similar seizures took place in May, when 12 live marine iguanas were found at Guayaquil’s airport (2) and four more were rescued from a residential area (1, 2). These reptiles, highly desired by exotic pet collectors, are endemic to the Galapagos Islands and classified as Vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (3). Ecuadorian law prohibits their removal (4), and the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) prohibits their international trade (5). The recent smuggling attempts reveal that Ecuador’s wildlife-detection control measures, such as x-ray baggage scanners (6, 7), are insufficient (2, 6). To protect marine iguanas, Ecuador must address the gaps in its wildlife trafficking policies.
